reachable: Yes, and reachable in the only way a batcher can be. The batcher is instantiated in evolve/harness.py::_train (G.load_batcher(genome)(fit_stripped, bs, seed)) and called once per step; the indices it returns select the sequences whose command/observation rows become the objective's rows and its in-batch negatives, so the mechanism gets gradient on every step of the run. All four mechanisms are live at the shipped params, verified by execution: (1) the identity-carrying backward walk labels all 24 real jail trajectories with deepest scores exactly {1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0} and excludes every accumulator read; (2) both cell cascades build cells and both channels are drawn (img 0.55 / geo 0.45); (3) the duplicate filter is active — on a 2880-sequence scale-up that preserves the real duplicate structure it cuts avoidable-class collision pairs per batch from 421 to 238; (4) the quasi-random sweep replaces multinomial in both the cell and sequence draws. The depth tilt bites at full ramp almost exactly as claimed: the deepest stratum takes 0.665 of exposure against a 0.333 population share and the shallowest 0.030 against 0.125 (hypothesis claimed 0.61/0.33 and 0.03/0.13). The batcher is never invoked at scoring time — cups_ca / cups_probe do not touch the batcher axis — so there is nothing to judge at the scored read position beyond what the training distribution does.
solves_outside_model: No leak. next_batch returns a plain list[int] of sequence indices and nothing else; the resolved routing (origin path, move-hop count, copy-hop count, cell key) never leaves the batcher's closure and is never written into tok / types / key_pad or into any tensor the net sees. Command parsing is used solely to compute a per-sequence sampling weight and a cell key — i.e. to choose SAMPLES, which the brief permits. z_obs is read only to build exact-duplicate classes for the assembly filter, again a sampling decision made at train time over training observations; the batcher does not run at scoring time and is not conditioned on the withheld answer at the probe's read position. I re-read the module end to end for a stamped-answer shape of the kind that caused the prior stream retraction and found none: there is no path from _identity_reads' output to any model input.
summary: The code implements all four advertised mechanisms and I could reproduce the author's headline measurements almost exactly. Mechanism 1 (backward identity-carrying walk, abandoning at an append) labels every one of the 24 real jail trajectories, with deepest scores spread over exactly {1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0} as claimed, recovers the origin path, and scores 0 accumulator reads where the partner scores 15. The jail-sample counts the author quotes — 8 images, 9 distinct read templates, 12 distinct origin templates — are exact. Mechanism 2's two cascades are keyed exactly as described. The contract claims all hold under real torch on a 2880-sequence split: exactly bs integer indices in range, distinct whenever n >= bs (0 repeats in 400 batches), deterministic given the seed, seed-sensitive, fit never mutated, private generator throughout, correct degradation with no routed read / no z_obs / n < bs / n == 1, no hang at n == bs, setup 0.11 s and 0.77 ms per step. The depth tilt reproduces to within a hair of the claimed numbers. What does not survive scrutiny is prose, not code: the accumulator example mislabels the partner's depth (1, not 2/3), "both parents use replacement=True" is wrong for the partner's member draw, the cross-image geo cells are summarized as "same board" when they are deliberately not, the mechanism-4 dispersion gain is about half what was claimed (0.958 vs 0.999, not 0.885 vs 0.997, and the sweep discards ~3/4 of its own Weyl positions because tick advances by the number drawn rather than consumed), and mechanism 3's stated effect is out of proportion to what it can reach — on real data only 6.2% of rows sit in an avoidable class while the single dominant unlearnable class, the empty observation every mv and redirect produces, is 36% of rows and is excluded by design. The author does flag that last one as failure mode #1, so it is disclosed rather than hidden, and I independently confirmed the underlying r12 focal diagnosis is real (duplicate rows retain ~3.9x the gradient of learned rows). Nothing here resolves routing into the model's input. I could NOT check: anything at real split scale — no encoded pack root exists on this machine, so cell populations, rejection rates and the dup_frac tilt trade-off at n in the thousands with genuinely distinct trajectories are unverified; my scale-ups replicate 24 trajectories and are degenerate in exactly the way the author warns about. I also could not reproduce the author's specific synthetic-split figures (540 -> 360 collisions, depth-4 0.65 -> 0.37) — on my structurally faithful split tightening dup_frac did not flatten the depth-4 share (0.665 -> 0.633). And I did not run training, so nothing about the score itself is checked — the author makes no score claim, which is correct.

divergences.claim: "[the partner] scores it as a depth-2/3 routed read and up-weights the sequence for it" — the motivating example for mechanism 1, about accumulator ('cat SRC >> acc.dat') reads.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The partner's rule is hops[b] = max(hops.get(b,0), hops.get(a,0)+1); the sN.dat sources are never themselves written, so every accumulator read in the real jail data is labelled depth 1, not 2 or 3. The substantive claim is still true: on the 24 jail trajectories the partner scores 15 accumulator reads as routed, this candidate scores 0.
divergences.evidence: Executed evolve/chunks/batcher/r2_routed_collision_depth_batcher.py::_routed_reads and the candidate's _identity_reads over evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl: partner total routed reads 74, of which 15 are '...acc.dat' at depth 1; candidate total identity reads 59, accumulator reads 0.

divergences.what_the_code_does: The parent does. The partner's cell draw does, but its member draw is torch.multinomial(member_w[bi], k, replacement=False, generator=g) — sampling without replacement inside a cell.

divergences.claim: Mechanism 2 cells are "the closest thing the training split contains to the role-swapped pair the metric compares against: same board, same destination, same depth, different content."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The geo channel's level-1 key is (digit-collapsed origin template, digit-collapsed read template, mv hops, cp hops) with NO image component — deliberately cross-image, so members are on different boards, not the same board. The hypothesis's own mechanical sentence two paragraphs earlier is accurate ("same shape of location ... differ only in which content that was, and on which system"); only the summary line overreaches. The same-board property belongs to the other channel (image-keyed), which carries 0.55 of the hard draw.
divergences.evidence: Candidate source lines 162-163 (img_levels vs geo_levels) and the channel split in make_batcher: img channel share = 1-geo_share = 0.55, geo channel 0.45.

divergences.claim: "Mechanism 3 stops the focal-weighted listwise term from spending itself on rows that are unlearnable by construction, which should raise the effective number of gradient steps that see a routed read at all inside the fixed budget."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code does exactly what it describes mechanically, but on the real observation distribution it can reach only a small minority of the unlearnable-duplicate mass. On the 24 real jail trajectories (724 command rows): 399 rows have a unique observation, 262 rows (36%) have the EMPTY observation — one class present in all 24 sequences, hence above avoid_frac and structurally excluded — 280 rows sit in other above-limit classes, and only 45 rows (6.2%) fall in an avoidable class. Mean per-sequence signature is 1.79 classes (6 of 24 sequences have an empty signature), while the rejection budget is max(dup_tol=3, 0.4*|sig|) = 3 for essentially every sequence, so a rejection requires 4+ already-present collisions from a signature that is usually 0-2 long. The author lists this as failure mode #1, so it is disclosed, but the causal claim above is not supported by the data that exists.
divergences.evidence: Measured directly on evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl: obs-text -> #sequences histogram {1:329, 2:11, 3:7, 12:1, 24:1}; limit at avoid_frac=0.25 is 6; 18 avoidable classes; signature sizes [1,0,1,2,2,4,3,4,2,4,5,4,1,0,0,0,2,4,1,0,1,0,1,1]. Separately confirmed the r12 focal diagnosis is real: with 16 of 64 rows exact duplicates, duplicate rows keep ~3.9x the gradient norm of learned unique rows as prediction error goes to zero.

divergences.claim: "Exposure-count dispersion under flat weights was 0.885 against 0.997 for iid sampling" (mechanism 4's variance reduction).
divergences.what_the_code_does: Isolating the global sweep (depth_beta=0, hard_frac_max=0, dup filter off) on a 2880-sequence split over 1000 steps gives dispersion 0.958 vs 0.999 for iid — real but roughly half the claimed improvement. The likely cause is visible in the code: the fill loop calls gsweep.draw(4*need+8) but stops offering after bs acceptances, while _WeightedSweep.draw advances self.tick by the full k, so about three quarters of each sweep's Weyl positions are generated and never consumed. The author already labels this mechanism "a real but modest variance reduction ... not the load-bearing part of this design".
divergences.evidence: /tmp/rev01/t5_disp.py; _WeightedSweep.draw increments self.tick += k regardless of how many of the k picks the caller consumes.
